1.Overview information:
A Lead represents a business person or organization interested in a company’s product or service. Leads can be converted into potential customers once qualified. You need to have the lead module enabled to access it. Please contact the Quoteplan support team if you want to activate it. Once the Lead module is enabled for your company’s Quoteplan instance, individual user need to have permission to View Lead module. 2.Creating a Lead

Steps to Create a Lead information:
Navigate to Menu → Lead → Create Lead. The Create Lead interface is displayed.

Enter the mandatory fields information:
First Name (of a person) Company Name (same as Person’s name if its a single person subcontractor without formal company name)

Enter basic lead information information:
Company URL

Shipping Address information:
If both addresses are the same, select “Copy Office Address to Shipping Address”. If the addresses are different, enter the shipping address separately. Lead status: by default put as not contacted, Lead source: enter information if known (this helps in analytics at a later stage). Lead status is a custom field, users can add new status or rename status that reflects the internal sales process. Sequence of Lead status is used in Lead analytics funnel chart.

Click Save. information:
The lead is saved successfully. Quoteplan checks if the same records already exist either in Lead module or Contact before creating a new Lead. Please see duplicate record check rules

Lead Module duplicate record check rules information:
Quoteplan tries to prevent duplicate records. If Lead email is found in the Lead Module then it gives the message ” Person with same Email ID already exists in Lead. If Lead email is found in the contact module , it gives the message” Person with same Email id already exists in Contacts.” If Lead name + company name already exists it gives message Company name + first name + last name of a contact person already exists in the lead list If the company URL is found in the Lead module, then it gives a message : This Company URL exists in the Lead. Do you want to create another Lead? If the company URL is found in the Business entity module, then it gives the message: This Company exists in Business Entity, do you want to create a new Lead?

Conversion Lead information:
On conversion, a Business Entity (Company) and a Contact (Person) are created on validation rules.

Business Entity (Company) Rules information:
If the Company URL exists and matches an existing Business Entity: The lead is merged into the existing Business Entity. If the Company URL does not exist:The system checks by Company Name. If Company Name does not exist: A new Business Entity is created. If Company Name exists once: The lead is merged into the existing Business Entity. If Company Name exists multiple times:◦ The user is prompted to either select an existing Business Entity to merge or create a new Business Entity.

Contact (Person) Rules information:
A new Contact is always created during lead conversion. If the Contact Email ID already exists, conversion is blocked with an error. If the combination of First Name + Last Name + Company Name or Company URL already exists: Conversion is blocked with an error. 8.1.Steps to Convert a Lead:(Convert a Lead into a Business Entity and Contact as per Conversion Rules) Click on the Menu.

Select Leads. information:

1. Introduction information:
The Timesheet module in Quotelan is designed to record the time spent by employees on different tasks, projects, or activities. It helps organizations track labor hours, billable and non-billable hours, leave, overtime (OT), double time (DT), triple time (TT), and payroll processes. Timesheet module is also used to track punch-in/punch-out (in and out entry) of every employee to the company. Timesheets can be created, modified, approved, rejected, reset, copied, and exported based on user permissions.

Weekly Timesheet Structure information:
Based on your company policy, you can initially decide the start day of the week. By default, Quoteplan shows Monday however this company setting can be changed before you start the timesheet module. The Timesheet module follows a weekly timesheet architecture, where users record working hours from Monday through Sunday. Each timesheet consists of multiple line items (rows). Every row represents a unique combination of Project, Labor, Task(optional), and Type.
Definition of Create and Save Timesheet. A functionality that allows users to create and save their timesheet for a selected week.
Create and Save Timesheet means A functionality that allows users to create and save their timesheet for a selected week.

Q: What is Create and Save Timesheet?
A: A functionality that allows users to create and save their timesheet for a selected week.
Create and Save Timesheet is used for Used for tracking work hours and managing time effectively.

Q: Why is Create and Save Timesheet used?
A: Used for tracking work hours and managing time effectively.

Create and Save Timesheet information:
In this functionality, a user can create and save their timesheet for a selected week.

Steps information:
Click on the Menu. Click on Time Tracking. Click on Create Timesheet. Select the required week using the Calendar Picker (Sunday to Saturday). By default Quoteplan shows current week Verify the selected week range and Today’s date displayed on the top-right corner. user can select 1 year prior today’s date or user can fill timesheet for 2 weeks in advance. User can fill a timesheet for PTO labor code 6 months in advance. For any other labor code, system will generate message You can only create and submit PTO 6 months in advance. Select a Project from the Project dropdown. User can see only specific projects for which user is assigned. User can select only labor codes assigned for that user for that project. Also user can select assigned tasks for that project. 10. User-labor, user-task, task-labor permissions are assigned in project module - project settings. 11. Select a Task from the Task dropdown. (if task is enabled for your timesheet) 12. Select Labor from the Labor dropdown. 13. Select Type from the dropdown (REG / OT / DT / TT). 14. Check or uncheck the Billable checkbox as required. 15. Enter hours (0–24) for each day in the respective hour fields. 16. Enter comments (maximum 500 characters) in the comment box. 17. Select the row checkbox if required. 18. Click on the Save Timesheet button.

2.1.1 System Behavior information:
The Timesheet is saved successfully. Status is displayed as No Status. Total hours are calculated automatically. Validation message is displayed if required fields are missing or daily hours exceed 24.

Triple Time information:
Total Time (not to exceed > 24 hrs per day)

Non-Billable Hours information:
PTO Hours (PTO labor code) Holiday Hours (Holiday labor code)

Total Hours information:
Hours Worked (=Total hrs - non payable) Non-Payable Hours (for Lunch and FMEA labor types only) Supplemental bonus (comes from numeric value written in comment section in timesheet. Eg: $100 for customer support - this will show 100 in supplemental bonus ) All calculations are dynamically recalculated whenever hours or configuration values change.

4. Row Management Behavior information:
After creating or opening a timesheet, users can add, edit, or delete rows. Row deletion is allowed before emailing the timesheet. After a row is deleted, all dependent calculated fields (such as Billable and Non-Billable hours) are recalculated automatically. When the Project field is changed in a row, all dependent fields (Labor, Task, Type, Hours, and Billable flag) are reset to avoid invalid data mapping. If a row contains zero hours, the system triggers a confirmation alert before saving. The Hours field accepts numeric values only

5. Viewing and Modifying Existing Timesheets information:
To modify an existing timesheet, the user accesses it through the View / Modify section. The user can change the timesheet anytime as long as the row is not locked. Once the timesheet is emailed, then the row becomes locked to prevent accidental changes. Users must explicitly unlock the timesheet using the Lock icon if user has permission If permission validation fails, the timesheet remains in read-only mode. Once changes are completed, the Save Timesheet action persists all updates.

7. Approval Workflow information:
No status to emailed to approved or rejected

In the Issue for Approval workflow information:
The user selects an approver (Supervisor, Client or Project Manager). If multiple rows are selected, then system automatically combines records and send to respective PM and Clients (records which belong to same PM or same Client will see only 1 email with multiple entries)

Upon submission, the system information:
Changes the timesheet status to “Emailed”, locks timesheet row Sends an email notification to the approver User can go into View/Modify Timesheet (search timesheet) page and see timesheet row status changed to Email. Hover mouse to see whom timesheet is emailed for approval. For supervisor or PM timesheet view: Moves the record to the Pending or Pending PM queue

If the user submits the timesheet for approval without saving it first information:
The system triggers an auto-save operation A confirmation prompt is displayed to avoid workflow state inconsistency

8. Approval Review & Status Updates information:
Supervisors and Project Managers review timesheets from their respective Pending tabs. or click on link received in email PM or Supervisor can approve / reject single timesheet at a time or bulk. For bulk approval/rejection, PM or supervisor must login to their respective Quoteplan timesheet module and navigate to Pending or Pending PM tab PM or Supervisor can write comments in the comment box to let user know reason On Approve or Reject, the system displays a confirmation popup. If timesheet is send to multiple levels of approval (supervisor AND PM and Client) then ALL of them MUST approve to change final status to Approved. If any of the approvers has rejected timesheet entry then it shows Rejected status

After confirmation information:
The timesheet status is updated (either approved or rejected) The originator receives an email notification The record is removed from the pending queue Timesheet gets locked and the user can not modify the timesheet any more. (only authorized user with permission can modify Approved timesheet)

If multiple Project Managers are assigned information:
Approval or rejection by one PM displays an approval indicator (tick mark). Hovering over the indicator reveals approver details.

9. Rejected Timesheet Handling information:
A rejected timesheet can be unlocked by the user using the locker toggle. Once unlocked, the timesheet becomes editable. The user can modify, save, and resubmit it for approval. User can not modify project however user can modify other attributes like labor, task, #of hrs, Type, Billable/non billable User can send modified timesheets for approval again. Status changes from Rejected to emailed.

10.1 The system uses a tab-based structure information:
Self – Displays the logged-in user’s timesheets Pending – Supervisor approval queue Pending PM – Project Manager approval queue All – Consolidated view of all records

10.2 Search and Advanced Search support information:
Multiple filters

11. PTO & Future Entries information:
The system supports PTO timesheet creation, allowing users to enter PTO for future dates. Future PTO creation is limited to a maximum of 6 months

12. Pagination & UI Controls information:
Pagination is implemented using a Load More mechanism. Each invocation loads the next 20 records. The Hide/Show Column feature allows users to control rows visibility at the UI level.

Current Stock Report Include following Columns  information:
Item ID: A unique identifier assigned to each inventory item. It is the primary reference for tracking, reporting, and system queries. Category: Indicates the product classification. Catalog Number: The manufacturer’s official reference or part number. Description: Provides detailed technical and functional information about the item. Make: Identifies the manufacturer (e.g., Allen-Bradley, Schneider). Unit: Primary unit of measurement used for inventory tracking. Unit2: Secondary unit of measurement, if applicable. Minimum Quantity: The minimum stock level required to avoid shortages. Quantity in Hand (Unit): Actual available stock measured in the primary unit. Quantity in Hand (Unit2): Actual available stock measured in the secondary unit. Location: Physical storage location such as a warehouse or site. Bin No: Specific bin, rack, or shelf number within the location to enable faster item retrieval. Landed Price:is the per-unit cost of an item calculated by dividing the total stock amount by the quantity in hand. It represents the actual cost of each unit currently available in stock. eg: if an item is bought at different price points and qty in hand shows item at different price points then Stock amount for that item = (purchase cost 1 * available qty 1) + (purchase cost 2 * available qty 2)….(purchase cost N * available qty N) Landed price = Stock amount of item / Total Qty in hand of that item Discounted Percent is fetched from Item Master. Discounted Price is fetched from Item Master Total Discounted Price this Price is derived by Multiplying discounted price of any Item with the Quantity in Hand List Price represents the standard listed price of the item The Stock Amount displays the total value of available stock, calculated based on the quantity in hand and the landed price. If the quantity in hand is zero, the item is considered out of stock Please Note That: Quantity and stock value of dummy items may not be correct

Stock on Previous Date report information:
The Stock on Previous Date report is a historical inventory report designed to display the stock position of items as it existed on a specific past date. This report helps users view inventory balances at any selected point in time, rather than showing current or stock. The system generates this report by analyzing all valid inventory transactions—such as purchases, issues, sales, and transfers—up to the selected date and excluding any transactions that occurred after that date. This report is especially useful for audit verification, reconciliation, and historical analysis, where accurate backdated stock information is required.

Stock By Project on Previous Date report information:
The Stock By Project on Previous Date report is a historical inventory report that displays the project-wise stock position of items as it existed on a specific past date selected by the user. This report helps users understand how much inventory was allocated or available for each project at a particular point in time, rather than showing current or livestock data. The system calculates this information by analyzing all inventory transactions—such as goods receipts, issues, transfers, and project allocations—up to and including the selected date, while excluding all transactions that occurred after that date. This report is especially important for project cost tracking, audit verification, historical reconciliation, and management review, where accurate backdated project-wise stock visibility is required.

In the system, an item is marked as rejected when information:
The material does not meet quality standards The delivered item does not match the purchase order specifications The quantity received is damaged, defective, or incorrect The item fails inspection or testing requirements

Generally your Quoteplan instance will have single or multiple BOM templates. There are 2 ways to create BOM information:
Menu - Project/ BOM - Create Project - copy and create, select source project(either master template or old project), click save and open BOM. It opens BOM. If copies source project BOM into current project (spreadsheet or folder type) Click on project, create normal project, click on Show BOM. It opens BLANK BOM (if its folder view, it shows Base folder with project name. If its spreadsheet BOM, it shows only 1 tab with BLANK spreadsheet) Populate items in BOM: there are various ways to insert items into BOM. Folder type BOM Using item master: open BOM - search item in left window item master, pick item (hold onto item icon) from left side and drop into right side window. When you drag an item and hover onto the base folder, it highlights the base folder in blue color, drop item and it gets inserted inside the base folder. If you drag an item and hold over any other folder on right side then it gives 2 options - copy inside or copy below. Copy inside will insert items inside the folder. Copy below will drop item below that folder. You can also drop item either above or below an existing item. User can not drop same item into same folder Using old BOM: open BOM - actions - Copy from BOM - Copy without Overwrite- search existing project, source BOM shows leftside in folder structure. Either pick the entire folder from the left side and drop into the right side or expand the left side BOM and then choose specific items and drop onto the right side.. User can not duplicate same item into same folder. If user picks entire folder then all sub folders and items inside those folders will get carried over as well. If you choose overwrite existing BOM option then existing BOM will get replaced by old selected BOM. Using BOM Import: open BOM - actions- Import BOM- select specific folder on which BOM should be imported, follow next steps to select source file from your local machine - map columns (catalog no or item id columns are mandatory)- next screen is preview screen: it shows which items are found in item master, which items are not found into item master- if you need to create new item click on first column select ALL checkbox , then click on Import and it will import file into current BOM. Please follow BOM import procedure for more details Spreadsheet type BOM Using item master: open BOM - search item in left window item master, pick item (hold onto item icon) from left side and drop into right side window. Based on user setting, when item is dropped into right side, it will either overwrite onto existing row or insert new row. Using old BOM: open BOM - actions - Copy from BOM - Copy without Overwrite- search existing project, source BOM shows leftside in folder structure. Expand left side folders and then drop items into right side. If you choose overwrite existing BOM option then existing BOM will get replaced by old selected BOM. Selecting source project BOM which is folder type: You can drag and drop items from this BOM or you can select entire folder to copy from. Selecting source project BOM which is spreadsheet type: You can drag and drop items from this BOM or you can select entire folder/tab to copy from. Quoteplan tracks and compares quantity, discounted price and global variables between different revisions. It highlights differences in Qty, Net Qty and Disc Price between old revision and next revision. If Qty or Disc Price has increased then it will highlight GREEN, if Qty or Disc Price has decreased then it will highlight in Light RED color. If New item has been added then it shows Green color, if an item is deleted then it shows in Light RED color. It also highlights difference between global BOM variables (Green color is price increased, Light Red color is price decreased) User can download difference between revisions in excel. If an offer letter/quote is sent in email via Quoteplan then you will see pdf attachment of Quote in revision comparison. Also you can download that BOM version in csv. Open Old revision user can open any old BOM revision. Actions- Open Revision - it shows list of all past revisions along with date and comments. User can click on Revision number and it opens that BOM revision. NOTE: old BOM revision opens on existing BOM view, so if you did not lock current BOM then all changes will be lost and you will not be able to retrieve those. Quoteplan gives you message : There are changes to this BOM since it was last locked. Opening another revision will discard those changes. Are you sure you want to open this revision?

Fetch Vendor Data information:
Quoteplan has the capability to link with vendors and fetch special prices and available stock at run time. We have partnered with various vendors and developed this feature. This feature is only enabled if your company has permission to fetch data from the vendor at real time. Actions- Fetch Vendor Data: Select single tab or multiple tabs- it opens next page and shows consolidated BOM for selected tabs. It shows preferred vendors linked to these items from item master. If you need to link items to vendor then Select rows, it shows Select Vendor menu - click on either preferred vendor 1 or preferred vendor 2 or Select from list. Preferred vendor 1 and 2 are coming from item master. If you click on Select from list, it will show you a list of all vendors who have partnered with us to fetch data. If your vendor name is not in the list then please contact us. Select rows- Actions - Fetch Distributor Data- select name of distributor. Quoteplan starts fetching various attributes : special price (your SPA or Disc Price or Purchase Cost) from the vendor, available stock (or lead time) , UPC code, item description, MPN (manufacture part number). It shows pending status till all item data is not retrieved, click on refresh to check status whether all data is complete or not. It changes to Done, when all item data is fetched. Parser status is true if data is fetched, parser status is false if that item is not available from the vendor or data is not received from the vendor. Once all data is received, then the user can push the latest discounted prices into the item master or into the current BOM. Synch item attributes into BOM Quoteplan allows user to sync various item attributes into current BOM. This is useful when user copies old project but wanted to apply latest prices from item master. Or if labor units have changed since BOM is created last time.

Preview Screen information:
this screen shows which items are found in Quoteplan item master and which items are not present. Quoteplan compares exact part number entered in csv/excel file, If found, it shows item id of item(s). if not found, it removes all special characters (like -, ‘ , “, ; , # ) and compares dashless catalog no as well. If not found then it shows item not found. User has an option to create new items on the fly. Item must be present in item master before it appears in BOM. If current BOM is not empty then Quoteplan also compares which items are present in existing BOM. If the current BOM has an item present however it does not exist in imported file then the Preview screen shows a message :<item id> Existing BOM Item. User can chose to keey qty of existing items by selecting the check box in the BOM Qty column . If user does not select the checkbox then the qty of the item in the existing BOM will reset to 0. User can also download preview screen result for reference and analysis. Click on Import to continue import operation. It shows confirmation message “If Item already exists in BOM: If you want to add BOM qty, click on Add Button. If you want to replace BOM qty with csv qty click on Replace button. If you do not want both, click on No button.” Once import is complete, click on Show BOM button to open BOM module. During Preview Screen, If user selected Add then it will show qty of BOM item has increased, if user selected Replace then current BOM qty is replaced by qty from imported file. Also notice that if user has selected to create new items on the fly then it new items are created in item master and inserted into BOM. Item attributes are collected from csv file. If description column is not mapped then catalog no is copied into item description. Ability to create new folders on the fly during BOM import

1. Introduction information:
The Expense Sheet module in QuotePlan allows employees to record and manage expenses incurred against assigned projects. This module helps organizations monitor, control, and reimburse employee expenses efficiently. Expense sheets can be created, modified, submitted for approval, approved, rejected, and exported based on user roles and permissions. This module supports a complete expense lifecycle with validation, approval workflows, attachments for proof, and reporting support. 2. Create and Save Expense Sheet Purpose: This functionality allows a user to create a new expense sheet and save it for later submission or approval.

2.1 Steps To Create and Save Expensesheet information:
1. Click on the Menu.

2. Select Expense Tracking. information:
3. Click on Create Expense Sheet. 4. Select a date using the calendar picker (Monday to Sunday). 5. Select a Project from the Project dropdown. 6. Select an Expense Type from the Expense dropdown. 7. Enter the Amount (manual or fixed, based on permissions). 8. Check the Reimbursable checkbox. 9. Add an Attachment as proof (mandatory for applicable expenses).

1. The expense sheet is saved successfully. 2. Status is displayed as No Status. 3. The total amount is calculated automatically. 4. Validation messages are shown if required fields are missing or invalid.

Introduction information:
A Sales Order (SO), also known as a Customer Sales Order or Customer Purchase Acknowledgement, is an internal document generated by the seller. It is created in response to a received Purchase Order (PO) from the customer. The Sales Order serves as a formal confirmation of the customer’s request and typically mirrors the details of the Purchase Order, including items, quantities, pricing, delivery terms, and milestone-based payment conditions, if applicable. Each line item in a Sales Order can be divided into payment milestones, such as Design, Build, and Deliver. Multiple milestone breakdowns are allowed for each line item to support progressive payments based on the completion of defined stages. A Sales Order (SO) is created to confirm customer requirements and define payment terms before invoicing. Follow the steps below to create and approve a Sales Order and then generate an Invoice from it. Steps to Create a Sales Order Step 1: Click on the Menu.

Step 3: Click Create Sales Order. information:
The Sales Order screen opens on the right side.

Fill in the following fields information:
ID: Auto-assigned by QuotePlan for internal reference. Sales Order No: Auto-generated and editable. Date: Displays the Sales Order creation date. Project: Select the project. The associated BOM appears on the left panel. Status: Displays the current Sales Order status. Buyer’s Order No / Customer PO No: Enter the Purchase Order number. Client PO Ref: Enter PO reference and PO date, if applicable. Delivery: Select FULL LOT or STAGGERED. Delivery Date: Enter delivery date as per PO. Inspection: Select Yes or No. Payment Terms: Enter agreed terms. Comments: Add remarks, if any. Attachments: Upload supporting documents.

Invoice Actions – Available Features information:
Generic Search: Keyword-based search can be performed on invoice columns such as Invoice No, Invoice Date, Customer, Project (No : Name), and Payment Terms, and only the records matching the selected search criteria are displayed. Column Filter: Invoices can be filtered by Invoice Number, Customer, Project, Status, and Due Date using filter criteria such as Equal (returns exact ), Like (returns records containing the entered value or partial value), and date-based Equal or Between for Due Date, with actions to apply filters, add multiple filters to refine results, and clear filters to reset the invoice listing. Export:Clicking on Export downloads the file invoice_data.csv, and all columns in the CSV exactly match the data displayed on the web page; when search or column filters are applied, only the searched or filtered records are exported and reflected correctly in the CSV file.. Load More: Display additional invoices beyond the current page without refreshing. Create New Invoice: Open the Create Invoice form to generate a new invoice.

1. Overview of Work Order in QuotePlan In QuotePlan, a Work Order is an optional module used as a trigger point for manufacturing activities. Some businesses use Work Orders to initiate production after receiving a customer purchase order. Other businesses may not require Work Orders, depending on their internal processes. Work Orders are commonly used together with Sales Orders, but Sales Orders are not mandatory in QuotePlan. QuotePlan is designed to support multiple business workflows with flexibility. 2. Relationship Between Sales Order and Work Order A Sales Order and Work Order usually go hand-in-hand, but this relationship is not compulsory.

A Work Order can be created information:

A Work Order is generally created information:
After receiving a customer purchase order To trigger manufacturing or production activities

If a customer orders a large quantity (for example, 1000 units) information:
It is not necessary to manufacture or ship everything at once. Production can be split into multiple batches over time using multiple Work Orders.

4. Multiple Work Orders Scenario information:
QuotePlan supports staggered manufacturing and delivery.

Typical Structure information:
One Project usually has one Sales Order One Sales Order can have multiple Work Orders

A customer orders 1000 units information:
Work Order 1: 200 units Work Order 2: Remaining units at a later stage This allows flexible planning and phased production. 5. Creating a Work Order in QuotePlan

Purchase Requisition (PR) is a formal internal document used to request the procurement of materials or services required for a project or operational activity. A Purchase Requisitions (PR) can be created in Quoteplan using multiple methods based on business requirements and user permissions. Users can create a Purchase Requisitions through the following ways information:
1. Purchase Requisitions (PR) Module: Users can directly create a Purchase Requisition by navigating to the Purchase Requisitions module and selecting Create PR.This method allows manual selection of suppliers, projects, and items. 2. Material Management (MM) Module: Purchase Requisitions can also be created from the Material Management (MM) module, where material requirements are managed project-wise. PRs created from MM supports additional functionalities such as vendor acknowledgment pricing and BOM price synchronization. Module Name : Purchase Requisitions (PR) – View Modify

View all created PR records Search, filter, and sort PR data Navigate to a specific PR for modification Perform actions such as export, email, comparison, PO creation, and BOM insertion Delete PRs based on status validation
